A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Linear Separability Ceiling study. Their complete text, tables, equations, figures, and Appendices A–M support reliable comparison despite the revised title, restructuring, and added evaluation.

before.justification: V1 reports original VLM evaluations, fine-tuning experiments, ablations, and generalization analyses on Bongard OpenWorld and Bongard-HOI.

after.justification: V2 retains original Bongard experiments, revises several results, and adds original zero-shot transfer results on Winoground in Table 7 and Appendix J.2.

M1.justification: The nearest-centroid probe, prompt/postfix tuning, and combined contrastive objective are retained. The diagnostic decision rule changes: v1 Section 4.2 distinguishes mechanisms by comparing generative and final-probe accuracy; v2 Section 5.2 instead tests whether final-probe accuracy also significantly exceeds the initial LSC.

E1.justification: V2 adds Winoground text and image retrieval, extending evaluation beyond Bongard few-shot visual rule classification to a different multimodal compositional task. Both original Bongard datasets remain, and models trained on each are evaluated on Winoground.

E2.justification: The eight-model baseline comparison is retained. V2 removes TPT and SVM-Mimic from the HOI split comparison and vision-bias tuning from the Phi intervention comparison. It adds CLIP ViT-L/14 as a Winoground comparator and human reference rows in Tables 1 and 6.

E3.justification: Appendix J.2 introduces zero-shot evaluation without task-specific adaptation, reporting separate Winoground text- and image-retrieval accuracies for Bongard-trained adapters. V2 also revises the statistical procedure determining whether models surpass the LSC. The original Bongard splits, checkpoint selection, and prompt-format evaluations remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 extends the existing transfer analysis by comparing OpenWorld versus HOI training and the two objectives on Winoground. It removes the vision-bias intervention ablation. The encoder ablation, prompt-format robustness tests, hyperparameter scan, class analysis, and attention-map studies are retained, with some Phi results revised.

E5.justification: V1 uses non-overlapping 95% confidence intervals to identify LSC surpassing; v2 uses a significance test based on the standard error of the difference at p < 0.05. V2 also adds uncertainty estimates to the existing HOI split and class-specific tables, while removing margins from collapsed Gemma representations. Neither version reports seeds or repeated-run counts.

E6.justification: V2 adds Winoground results and revises Phi scores throughout the main and appendix tables: OpenWorld LoRA LNT accuracy changes from 89.8% to 92.2%, while Lcombined changes from 96.2% to 95.6%. Under the revised diagnostic rules, reported baseline successes change from 4 refinement plus 10 non-linear cases to 2 plus 22. The underlying baseline accuracy table is unchanged; these counts do not indicate improved baseline performance.

T1.justification: The operational mathematical conditions defining the two successful mechanisms change: v2 requires both generative and final-probe accuracy to exceed the LSC for enhanced separability, replacing v1's generative/final-probe agreement criterion. The prototype construction, contrastive-loss definition, and scheduling equations remain unchanged, and no new proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: V1 foregrounds dormant reasoning pathways, task-dependent interventions, the shifting bottleneck, and structural brittleness. V2 makes the combined-objective fine-tuning method a central contribution, adds claims of exceeding human OpenWorld accuracy, and emphasizes more robust, transferable gains. Structural brittleness remains documented but is no longer a headline contribution.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the two mechanisms as extended bottom-up perception versus top-down decision logic, and emphasizes relational training as the source of transferable skills. It newly interprets prompt-format failures as catastrophic forgetting and loss of general reasoning heuristics. V1's stronger inference that the remaining perceptual limitation is architectural is removed.

D1.justification: V2 newly describes LoRA targets as attention and MLP layers, although Appendix G retains an attention-layer description; the PDFs do not clearly establish whether implementation changed. Vision-bias configuration details are removed. Learning rates, batch sizes, adapter rank/scaling, soft-prompt specifications, temperature, and loss schedules otherwise remain documented as before.

R1.justification: The positioning shifts substantially toward perception/reasoning alignment and training objectives. V2 adds linear-transferability and stochastic-separation literature, architectural and reinforcement-learning alternatives, and an explicit distinction between its image-to-image alignment and prior image-to-text alignment. The mechanistic-interpretability subsection and several benchmark-related references are removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, diagnostic explanation, discussion, and conclusion undergo extensive rewriting. V2 adopts alignment-gap terminology, adds an LLM Usage section, merges activation/adaptation discussion into the intervention section, and reorganizes generalization and limitations. Appendix J gains separate cross-Bongard and Winoground subsections.

P2.justification: V1's framework flowchart is removed, and its scatter plot is redrawn with statistical decision regions and revised legends. V2 adds summary and Winoground tables, redisplays existing dependence and activation findings, changes table emphasis conventions, and restructures the HOI split table. The task illustration, hyperparameter plot, and attention-map images are unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful cross-task evidence and fuller uncertainty reporting, but removes the TPT/SVM-Mimic comparisons and makes broader robustness and transfer claims. Those claims are only partly supported: prompt-format failures persist, and Table A.7 shows HOI-trained Pixtral image retrieval at 24.75% with LNT versus 12.25% with Lcombined, despite stronger text retrieval. The expanded evidence and less consistently qualified conclusions leave the net quality change uncertain.
